mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day period with similar FEDFUNDS trajectory (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% while UNRATE falls by 0.5 percentage points within the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future profits and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeding 0.3% for three consecutive months (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp drop in inventory levels (implied via a large negative monthly change in GDPC1) indicates supply-side stress, which can trigger a short-term S&P 500 bearish reaction over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% while GDPC1 decreases by > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of stable supply conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains below 1.5% for three consecutive months during a non-recessionary regime, it signals accommodative policy, which tends to boost equity valuations and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for three consecutive months and UNRATE < 4.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the policy signal (IC < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-standard-deviation increase in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests strong job creation, which can drive risk-on sentiment and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least one standard deviation above its 12-month mean while UNRATE remains unchanged
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the payroll surge (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% in a tightening cycle is interpreted as a deflationary signal that can depress growth expectations and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.4 percentage points in a month when FEDFUNDS is rising
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during prior deflationary periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) lags the prior month by more than 6% while inventory levels (inferred from GDPC1) show no meaningful change, it indicates a supply shock that can lead to a sharp decline in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 6% while GDPC1 change is within ±1% of previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant deviation from a baseline of stable supply conditions (IC < -0.15).
